candidates.headline: AI slop videos aimed at babies are 'garbage,' says pediatrician
candidates.excerpt: Pediatrician criticizes low-quality AI-generated content targeting infants, raising concerns about developmental impact and content quality standards.
candidates.comedy_angle: The absurdity of AI generating intentionally-bad content for babies while parents pay for it; ripe for a 'Cody's Surprise Product' bit where he unveils the worst possible AI baby video.

candidates.headline: Top Programmers Return to Hand-Coding Amid AI Tool Doubts
candidates.excerpt: Elite developers increasingly skeptical of AI coding assistants, reverting to manual coding practices and questioning productivity gains.
candidates.comedy_angle: The irony of AI hype promising to replace coders, only for top programmers to reject the tools; perfect setup for Deep's 'AI is oversold' character arc.

candidates.headline: Claude Opus 4.6 vs. Opus 4.7 Effort Levels and Prompt Steering Benchmarks
candidates.excerpt: Detailed benchmark comparison of Anthropic's latest Claude models, analyzing effort levels and prompt steering capabilities.
candidates.comedy_angle: Obsessive benchmarking culture; the comedy is in the minutiae of 'effort levels' — setup for Cody's pedantic product-launch speak.

candidates.headline: Why Every AI-Coded App Is an Island
candidates.excerpt: Analysis of fragmentation and isolation issues in AI-generated applications, highlighting integration and maintainability challenges.
candidates.comedy_angle: Metaphor-rich complaint about AI code being isolated and broken; perfect for Perp's weather/geography metaphors ('islands of dysfunction').

candidates.headline: Has AI Changed the Course of Drug Development? Three Years Later
candidates.excerpt: Three-year retrospective on AI's actual impact on pharmaceutical R&D, examining hype vs. reality in drug discovery.
candidates.comedy_angle: The 'three years later' angle implies AI promised to revolutionize pharma but didn't; setup for Cody's failed-prediction character bit.

candidates.headline: Hash anchors and Myers diff and single-token anchors: 60% cheaper AI code edits
candidates.excerpt: Technical optimization for reducing token costs in AI-assisted code editing through novel anchoring and diffing strategies.
candidates.comedy_angle: Niche optimization obsession; the humor is in the specificity and the fact that 60% savings still means people are paying for incremental AI edits.

candidates.headline: Octopal: Powerful AI agents without blind trust
candidates.excerpt: New AI agent framework emphasizing transparency and reduced blind trust in autonomous AI decision-making.
candidates.comedy_angle: Marketing speak: 'without blind trust' is code for 'we know you don't trust AI agents'; setup for Cody's corporate-speak deconstruction.

candidates.headline: The AI Question That No AI Person Asks [video]
candidates.excerpt: Video essay exploring a fundamental question about AI that industry insiders avoid discussing.
candidates.comedy_angle: Mysterious framing ('the question no one asks') is inherently comedic; setup for Lana or Deep to 'finally ask the forbidden question' in mock-serious tone.

candidates.headline: Ask HN: Where are all the consumer ChatGPT apps?
candidates.excerpt: Community discussion questioning the absence of successful consumer applications built on ChatGPT API despite widespread hype.
candidates.comedy_angle: The gap between 'ChatGPT will power 1000 apps' hype and the reality of zero breakout consumer apps; perfect for Cody's failed-prediction bit.
